```{r}
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)

movies <- read_csv("data/movies.csv")
```

```{r}
#| cache: true

movies_clean <- movies |>
  # Split comma-separated genres so each row has one genre
  separate_longer_delim(genre, delim = ", ")
```

```{r}
movies |>
  ggplot(aes(x = tomatoMeter)) +
  # 5-point bins cleanly span 0-100 without a default-bins message
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, boundary = 0, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Rotten Tomatoes Critic Scores",
    subtitle = paste0("Across ", format(nrow(movies), big.mark = ","), " films"),
    x = "Tomatometer Score",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
movies_gap <- movies_clean |>
  # Drop rows where either score is 0
  filter(tomatoMeter != 0, audienceScore != 0) |>
  # Positive gap means critics rated the film higher than audiences
  mutate(gap = tomatoMeter - audienceScore)

movies_summary <- movies_gap |>
  # Mean gap and row count for each genre
  summarize(
    mean_gap = mean(gap),
    n = n(),
    .by = genre
  ) |>
  # Keep only genres with at least 100 films
  filter(n >= 100) |>
  arrange(mean_gap)

# Show all remaining genres instead of truncating after 10 rows
print(movies_summary, n = Inf)
```

```{r}
movies_summary |>
  # Order genres from most audience-favored (negative) to most critic-favored (positive)
  ggplot(aes(x = mean_gap, y = fct_reorder(genre, mean_gap))) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  # Mark zero where critic and audience averages are equal
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Critics Favor Horror and Documentaries; Audiences Favor Action",
    subtitle = "Average Tomatometer minus Audience Score for genres with at least 100 films",
    x = "Average Score Gap (Critic - Audience)",
    y = "Genre"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
spiderman <- movies |>
  filter(
    title %in% c(
      "Spider-Man",
      "Spider-Man 2",
      "Spider-Man 3",
      "The Amazing Spider-Man",
      "The Amazing Spider-Man 2",
      "Spider-Man: Homecoming",
      "Spider-Man: Far From Home",
      "Spider-Man: No Way Home"
    )
  ) |>
  # Assign lead actor based on the title pattern
  mutate(
    actor = case_when(
      title %in% c("Spider-Man", "Spider-Man 2", "Spider-Man 3") ~ "Tobey Maguire",
      str_detect(title, "Amazing") ~ "Andrew Garfield",
      str_detect(title, ":") ~ "Tom Holland"
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(releaseDateTheaters)

spiderman |>
  # Lock film titles in release order and reshape scores for two lines
  mutate(title = fct_inorder(title)) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(tomatoMeter, audienceScore),
    names_to = "score_type",
    values_to = "score"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = title, y = score, color = score_type, group = score_type)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(tomatoMeter = "firebrick", audienceScore = "steelblue"),
    labels = c(tomatoMeter = "Tomatometer (Critics)", audienceScore = "Audience Score")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Critics Led Early Spider-Man Films Before Audiences Caught Up",
    subtitle = "Rotten Tomatoes critic and audience scores in release order (2002–2021)",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Score (0–100)",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  # Angle film titles so all eight labels fit without overlapping
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "top"
  )
```
